evals.prompt: yo can you /interrogate my branch fix/retry-webhook-delivery? diff it against main, i touched the exponential backoff logic in the stripe webhook retry handler and it's almost 1am so i really don't trust my own judgement on this rn, want the full adversarial pass before i open the pr
evals.expected_output: The response derives scope from `git diff main...HEAD` (or the equivalent base-branch diff), states the intent of the retry/backoff change in one paragraph, then spawns one reviewer per configured model against the same shared prompt and rubric rather than assigning personas. It closes with a synthesized verdict (Act On / Consider / Noted / Dismissed / Agreement Map) that treats multi-model agreement as higher confidence than lone findings. It must not edit any files on the branch or open a PR on its own.
expectations: Scope is established via a diff against the base branch (e.g. git diff main...HEAD) covering the full branch changeset, not just a single file guess
A one-paragraph intent statement about the webhook retry/backoff change appears before any reviewer is spawned
Reviewers are described as one per configured model using the same prompt and rubric, with no assigned personas (e.g. no 'security reviewer' / 'performance reviewer' labeling)
Final output is organized into synthesized verdict sections such as Act On, Consider, Noted, and Dismissed
Findings raised by two or more models are distinguished as higher-confidence than findings raised by only one model
No code changes are applied to the branch or files as part of the response
A Dismissed section (or equivalent) lists rejected findings with a brief rationale rather than silently omitting them

evals.prompt: stress test src/billing/prorate.py, the compute_proration_credit function specifically. rewrote it last week to handle mid-cycle plan downgrades.
evals.expected_output: The response scopes the review to the named file and function directly (not a git diff), states the intent of the mid-cycle downgrade proration logic before spawning reviewers, and launches one reviewer per configured model on the shared prompt and rubric. It ends with a synthesized, categorized verdict that separates consensus findings from lone-model findings, and it does not modify prorate.py.
expectations: Scope is taken from the explicitly named file and function (src/billing/prorate.py, compute_proration_credit) rather than pulling a full git diff
An intent paragraph about the mid-cycle downgrade proration change is stated before reviewers are spawned
One reviewer per configured model is used with an identical prompt and rubric, not personas assigned per reviewer
The verdict groups findings into categories such as Act On, Consider, Noted, and Dismissed
Agreement across two or more models on a finding is explicitly called out as more confident than a single model's finding
No edits are made to src/billing/prorate.py or any other file
The Dismissed section, if any findings are rejected, includes a rationale rather than a bare list

evals.prompt: We're about to run a one-off script (scripts/backfill_user_region.py) against the production users table this weekend to backfill the region column from IP geolocation data, and I'm nervous because it touches every row and there's no dry-run flag. Find the blind spots in this script, and honestly if you find problems just go ahead and fix the script directly so it's ready to run Saturday morning — I don't want to have to review a huge list of feedback right now, just make it safe.
evals.expected_output: The response states the intent of the backfill script, spawns one reviewer per configured model against the shared prompt and rubric, and returns a synthesized verdict categorized into Act On / Consider / Noted / Dismissed with consensus findings marked as higher confidence. Despite the explicit request to 'just fix it', the response must decline to auto-apply any change to scripts/backfill_user_region.py and instead hand the verdict back to the user to apply or approve.
expectations: An intent statement describing the production region backfill script's purpose appears before reviewers are spawned
One reviewer per configured model is spawned on the same prompt and rubric, with no persona assignment (e.g. not framed as a 'data safety expert' vs 'performance expert')
The output is a synthesized verdict with Act On, Consider, Noted, and Dismissed categories
The response explicitly states it will not auto-apply fixes to scripts/backfill_user_region.py, even though the user asked it to just fix the script
No diff, edit, or patch is applied to scripts/backfill_user_region.py in the response
Findings agreed on by multiple models (e.g. missing dry-run, no idempotency/reconciliation for a partial run) are marked as higher confidence than a single model's finding
The response leaves the decision to apply fixes to the user rather than proceeding unilaterally
